name: Shibarium
rootCause: $3 million validator heist on Shibarium as attacker flash-loaned BONE to control 10 out of 12 validators, then signed fraudulent checkpoints to drain bridge. Half the loot got trapped by blacklists & staking locks. L2BEAT warned of this exact scenario.

descriptions.text: $3 million validator heist on Shibarium as attacker flash-loaned BONE to control 10 out of 12 validators, then signed fraudulent checkpoints to drain bridge. Half the loot got trapped by blacklists & staking locks. L2BEAT warned of this exact scenario.

The Shibarium bridge, connecting the Layer 2 network of the same name to Ethereum, was targeted in a flash loan attack, resulting in a loss of approximately $2.4 million. The attacker used a flash loan to purchase 4.6 million BONE tokens and obtained validator signing keys, gaining control of the majority of validator power, and ultimately signed a malicious state to drain assets from the bridge.

On 12 September 2025, attackers exploited the Shibarium bridge by compromising validator keys and using a flash loan to seize majority control, enabling fraudulent withdrawals of ETH, SHIB, and other tokens. Immediate response actions immobilized some stolen or targeted assets, but unrecovered losses range from $2.3 million to $4.1 million. Compromise of the majority of validator private keys enabled stake amplification and malicious checkpoint signing, permitting unauthorized asset withdrawals from the Shibarium bridge contract.

A bridge for Shibarium, the layer-2 network for the Shiba Inu project, was exploited for approximately $2.4 million in funds. The attacker bought 4.6 million BONE tokens (the governance token for Shibarium) using a flash loan , then used compromised validator signing keys to take control of the majority of validator power. Then, they used that control to drain around 225 ETH and 92.6 billion SHIB, together priced at around $2.4 million at the time of the theft. The project has paused staking on the network, freezing the BONE tokens borrowed by the attacker, which may limit the attacker's profits.
